newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Surgical cuts Circon offer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Surgical cuts Circon offer.

text.p: U.S. Surgical Corp. said Monday it was lowering its offer for Circon Corp. in an effort to secure a friendly merger agreement but added it was willing to pursue its hostile takeover bid for the company.

Norwalk, Conn.-based U.S. Surgical said it was now offering $14.50 a share in cash, or about $14 million, for 14.9 percent of Circon stock, the amount it can buy without triggering an anti-takeover "poison pill" set up by Circon.

Circon, based in Santa Barbara, Calif., put the "poison pill" in place after U.S. Surgical launched its bid for the company, which makes advanced endoscopes and miniature colour video systems for medical and industrial applications.
U.S. Surgical's latest offer will expire at midnight July 14. After that, the company said it will offer $16.50 a share for all outstanding shares in an offer valued at $230 million.

"Hopefully, (Circon) management will say, 'Hey, U.S. Surgical's not going away, let's sit down and talk to them,'" U.S. Surgical spokeswoman Marianne Scipione said by telephone. "But if they don't, we fully intend to ... go back up to $16.50 (per share)."

U.S. Surgical, the world's largest independent maker of surgical staples and sutures, also said it was considering a proxy contest to nominate two directors to Circon's board of directors to help its takeover effort.

U.S. Surgical has been trying to acquire Circon since August, when it offered $18 a share for all outstanding shares in a deal it valued at $250 million. In December, the company lowered its offer to $17 a share in a bid worth $240 million.

"We believe this will send a clear message to Circon's management and the market that USS believes the immediate merger of these two synergistic companies is in the best interest of both companies and their respective shareholders," U.S. Surgical Chairman Leon Hirsch said in a statement.
"With the passage of time, not only has Circon's management been unable to achieve better operating results, but Circon's performance continues to be below even historical levels," Hirsch said.

"Based upon results for the past three quarters, USS can no longer justify to its shareholders -- absent the ability to review and discuss with Circon's management its operating plan -- an offer of $17 per share," Hirsch said.
Eva Snitkin, an analyst at Montgomery Securities in San Francisco, said, "I've been surprised all along that Circon has fought the takeover as hard as they have.
"In retrospect, that first offer (of $18) now looks pretty sweet," Snitkin said. "It seems to continually get worse at Circon, yet they have a very good franchise in urology."
Circon shares rose 75 cents to $13.50 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq. U.S. Surgical rose 25 cents to $34 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
